creator: Dan McCreary

Audio

Frequency Response

dublinCore.description: Frequency response of an amplifier's bass and treble controls, drawn as gain in dB against log frequency, with two sliders and a mouse probe that reads the gain.
relation: Chapter 15: Signal Processing Applications and AI Integration

learningObjectives: Predict the boost or cut in dB at the low and high ends of the response from the Bass and Treble slider positions, using 12(slider-50)/50 dB
Interpret a logarithmic frequency axis by counting octaves between two frequencies on the plot
Convert a gain in dB read from the plot into an amplitude ratio, for example +12 dB to about 4 times and -12 dB to about 0.25 times
Explain why the gain at a shelf corner is half of the full shelf gain
Analyze how the two shelves overlap near 1 kHz, so that the bass control also changes the middle of the spectrum
prerequisites: Frequency in hertz and the idea of a spectrum
A first look at the decibel scale

misconceptions.misconception: +6 dB makes a sound twice as loud
misconceptions.correction: +6 dB doubles the amplitude (and quadruples the power); about +10 dB is needed for a sound to seem twice as loud
misconceptions.evidence: Bass = 75 reads +6 dB (amplitude times 2) and Bass = 100 reads +12 dB (amplitude times 4): each extra 6 dB doubles the amplitude again

misconceptions.misconception: The bass control only changes the bass
misconceptions.correction: The shelves are smooth and overlap, so each control also changes the middle of the spectrum slightly
misconceptions.evidence: With both sliders at 100 the probe at 1 kHz reads +1.4 dB although 1 kHz is far from both corners

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Frequency response plot of a bass and treble tone control. A blue curve shows gain in decibels from minus 15 to plus 15 against frequency from 20 hertz to 20 kilohertz on a logarithmic axis. The bass slider boosts or cuts frequencies below 500 hertz and the treble slider boosts or cuts frequencies above 2 kilohertz. Moving the mouse over the plot reads the gain at any frequency.

controls.label: Bass
controls.description: Boosts or cuts frequencies below the 500 Hz corner by up to 12 dB; 50 is flat

controls.label: Treble
controls.description: Boosts or cuts frequencies above the 2 kHz corner by up to 12 dB; 50 is flat

visualElements.description: Gain in dB versus frequency (20 Hz to 20 kHz, logarithmic axis) with a 0 dB reference line and dotted lines at the 500 Hz and 2 kHz corners
Gold probe marker that follows the mouse along the frequency axis and sits on the curve
Probe read-out of frequency and gain, and the full shelf gain in dB beside each slider

model.description: Gain in dB is the sum of a low shelf (corner 500 Hz) and a high shelf (corner 2 kHz), each scaled by up to 12 dB; magnitude only, no audio

instructionalStrategies: Predict-then-verify with the sliders and the probe
extensions: Add a playable tone or noise source so the effect can be heard
